correctness.rationale: The group commutator is the alternating form B on the 2n-dimensional quotient. For every nonzero quotient vector v, conjugation changes the central coordinate by the nonzero functional u->B(u,v), which is surjective, so each noncentral conjugacy class is exactly the q-element fiber C_v and CCC adjacency is B(v,w)=0. Partitioning nonzero vectors into projective lines gives K_{q-1} blocks and the complement of Tang--Wan Sp(2n,q) between blocks. Orthogonal-space dimensions give degree, diameter and the q=2 versus q>2 common-neighbor counts; a clique spans a totally isotropic subspace of dimension at most n, with equality from a Lagrangian. Applying the standard K_{q-1} lexicographic eigenvalue transform to the inspected projective spectrum yields the displayed spectrum and multiplicities.
risks: The n=1 prime-field boundary is prior center-index-p^2 territory and is explicitly excluded from the originality claim.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a complete structural and spectral description for a standard infinite family of finite Heisenberg groups, translating group conjugacy into symplectic geometry. Exact diameter, clique number, integral spectrum and the sharp q=2 versus q>2 strong-regularity transition are natural reusable consequences, not a tiny isolated computation.
risks: The projective spectrum is inherited prior input rather than a new spectral computation from first principles.

limitations: The theorem is for the standard one-dimensional-center Heisenberg family; more general class-two groups can have vector-valued commutator maps.
